names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 iunie, «Sfânta Muceniță Achilina».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Ιουνίου, «Αγία Ακυλίνη», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 13. јун ст. ст., „Света мученица Аквилина“ — Света is not a rank and мученица is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the bare forename is left, which is all the heading gives. `foldchk.py` holds no folder on «Аквилина», so there is no fold.

Read out of the name link behind the calendar's line for 13 июня ст. ст., name page 2375, «Акилина Старшая, Библская (Финикийская), мц.», with the rank word left off. Старшая, the elder, is kept because it is what the calendar uses to tell her from the other Aquilina; the line itself gives the forename alone and in the genitive.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 июня ст. ст. — «Мц. Акилины (293).»

attestations.note: The day's first entry. The same menologion number this folder's romanian, greek and serbian rows already carry, so there is no second day and no note is owed. The line gives 293, the year the folder already holds off the Охридски пролог, and the Russian life repeats it in words, «(+ 293)»; `dates` was not touched. Her life page, life1294, was READ WHOLE and tells the passion the folder already holds from three books; the one thing it adds is the translation of her relics to Constantinople into a church built in her honour, which is the new paragraph. Two of the day page's eight hymns are taken: «Тропарь мученицы Акилины» глас 4, which is THE COMMON OF A WOMAN MARTYR with her name set in it — the folder already holds the same common in Romanian from doxologia and this is the Slavonic of it — and «Кондак мученицы Акилины» глас 2, which is proper to her. Not checked: azbyka.ru.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 iunie — «Sfânta Muceniță Achilina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Ιουνίου — «Αγία Ακυλίνη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. It is plainly the same girl: the child of a rich and noble house in Palestine under Diocletian, baptised at five by the bishop Euthalios, whose father was Eutolmios, who preached while still young, was denounced to the proconsul Volusianus, struck in the face, tortured and beheaded. saint.gr writes the proconsul's name «Ουλοσιανό» and gives no year. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.06.2026 (13. јун ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Аквилина“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 13 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated row carries, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. A FIRST DATE ON A FOLDER THAT HELD NONE. The folder carried no `dates` object at all. This book states one flat and last: „А пострада и увенча се венцем мученичким 293. године“. `death` 293 to 293, display «293», basis traditional, the Prologue’s own sentence in the note. **No `birth`, and the entry hands one over almost ready**: it says „Беше светој Аквилини дванаест година од рођења када пострада за Господа“ — she was twelve when she suffered. Twelve from two hundred and ninety-three is a year reached by arithmetic and a lifespan besides, and both are refused; the twelve years are stated in the life as the book states them and no year of birth is written. WHAT ELSE IS NEW, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF HER PASSION. Born in the Palestinian city of Byblos of honourable Christian parents, which is the place the folder’s display name already carries; fully taught the Christian life in her seventh year and in her tenth so full of divine understanding and the grace of the Holy Spirit that she preached Christ to her companions with great force; informed against to the imperial governor Volusian when Diocletian’s persecution began; scourged, then a red-hot rod driven through her ears and her brain; confessing Christ freely and openly to the last hour, and falling as dead when brain and blood ran from her head; carried out of the city and thrown on a dunghill for the dogs; an angel of God raising her in the night with „Устани, буди здрава!“; her prayer not to be denied the finishing of her contest and the voice from heaven „Иди, биће ти, како молиш!“; the city gate opening of itself before her; her coming in like a spirit to the governor’s own bedside and his unspeakable terror at a living girl he held for dead; the executioners led out next day, her kneeling prayer, and that **she gave up her spirit before the stroke and the executioner beheaded her dead** — which is why the entry’s own order is kept in the life. And that her relics gave healing to many sick. `types` UNTOUCHED: `martyr` and `virgin` are both there already, мученица in the heading is the first and девица in the body is the second, which the folder had from elsewhere. NO ROWS for Volusian, a pagan governor with no folder, nor for Diocletian, an emperor in a life taking no row for being one, nor for the parents or the companions, who are unnamed. No `office`, no `locations`, no `related`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Achilina, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Achilina; the common troparion of a woman martyr, with her name set in it. The lower-case «pentru tine» in the page's fourth clause is the page's own reading.

english.text: Thy lamb, O Jesus, Aquilina, crieth out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; and I am crucified with Thee and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; and I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign in Thee; and I die for Thee, that I may live for Thee. Receive me, then, as a sacrifice without blemish, who with love offer myself to Thee. At her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Παρθένος ἀκήρατος καὶ ἀθληφόρος σεμνὴ ἐδείχθης τοῖς πέρασι τῇ ἀγαπήσει Χριστοῦ, Ἀκυλίνα θεόνυμφε· σὺ γὰρ καθάπερ ῥόδον νοητὸν τεθηλυῒα, ἐπνεύσω ἐν ἀθλήσει τῆς ἁγνείας τὴν χάριν πρεσβεύουσα τῷ Κυρίῳ σῴζεσθαι ἅπαντας.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Αγία Ακυλίνη», and the one that names her; the second, «Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ», is the common of a woman martyr

english.text: An undefiled virgin and a modest bearer of the prize were you shown to the ends of the earth by your love of Christ, O Aquilina, bride of God; for having blossomed like a spiritual rose, you breathed out in your contest the fragrance of purity, interceding with the Lord that all may be saved.

hymns.text: Ραντισμοῖς αἱμάτων σου, καθηγνισμένην παρθένε, καὶ Μαρτύρων στέμμασι, σὲ Ἀκυλίνα στεφθείσαν, δέδωκε, τοῖς ἐν ἀνάγκαις τῶν νοσημάτων, ἴασιν, καὶ σωτηρίαν ὁ σὸς νυμφίος, τοῖς προστρέχουσιν ἐν πίστει, Χριστὸς ὁ βρύων ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, on the page of «Αγία Ακυλίνη», and it names her

english.text: You, O virgin Aquilina, hallowed by the sprinkling of your own blood and crowned with the martyrs' garlands, your bridegroom Christ, who wells up eternal life, has given for healing and salvation to those hard pressed by sickness who run to you in faith.

hymns.text: Агница Твоя, Иисусе, Акилина/ зовет велиим гласом:/ Тебе, Женише мой, люблю,/ и, Тебе ищущи, страдальчествую,/ и сраспинаюся, и спогребаюся крещению Твоему,/ и стражду Тебе ради,/ яко да царствую в Тебе,/ и умираю за Тя, да и живу с Тобою,/ но яко жертву непорочную приими мя,/ с любовию пожершуюся Тебе.// Тоя молитвами, яко Милостив, спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь мученицы Акилины»

english.text: Your lamb, O Jesus, Aquilina, cries out with a loud voice: you, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking you I suffer, and I am crucified with you and buried with you in your baptism; and I suffer for your sake, that I may reign in you, and I die for you, that I may live with you. Receive me then as a sacrifice without blemish, who with love have offered myself to you. At her prayers, as you are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Девства твоего добротами предочистивши душу твою,/ на высоту мучением востекла еси,/ Акилино всечестная,/ любовию Жениха твоего Христа уязвившися,/ Емуже со Ангелы предстоиши, веселящися,// с нимиже не престай моляся о всех нас.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак мученицы Акилины»

english.text: Having cleansed your soul beforehand with the beauties of your virginity, you ascended to the height by martyrdom, O all-honoured Aquilina, wounded with love for Christ your Bridegroom, before whom you stand with the angels and rejoice; cease not to pray together with them for us all.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 13. јун ст. ст. ends the entry „А пострада и увенча се венцем мученичким 293. године“. The folder held no date of any kind before this: neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr gave a year. The same entry says she was twelve years old when she suffered; no year of birth is taken from that, because it would be both a lifespan and a year reached by arithmetic (5 October 2026).
